Hi Rajesh — thanks, and welcome.

We reviewed the SOW and diagram; overall this looks straightforward. Quick commitments from our side:
- Redwood will provide a short preflight checklist and runbook before your connectivity window (I listed items below).
- We need the CIDR blocks and NAT/eBPF gateway details by EOD July 4 so our infra can pre-provision routes and firewall rules.
- We'll confirm the outbound IP set and a stable egress IP per region by July 5.

Preflight / runbook highlights (we'll send the full doc on Friday):
1) Account setup: service account names, allowed roles, and minimal privileges required.
2) Network: required ports, recommended routing (VPC peering vs managed interconnect), MTU/cross-region concerns.
3) Security: KMS key fingerprints for envelope encryption, logging endpoints, and retention expectations.
4) Tests: TCP/UDP port sweep, TLS handshake validation, sample token exchange, KV cache seeding check.

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical handoff on Friday July 6 at 10:00am PT? I'll bring Karthik and Ben (network and infra). If that slot doesn't work for you, propose an alternative.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 2, 2028 at 11:05 AM maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai wrote:
> Preflight / runbook highlights (we'll send the full doc on Friday):
> 1) Account setup: service account names, allowed roles, and minimal privileges required.

Hi Rajesh — looping in a short technical checklist so you can prepare items in parallel. I kept this minimal so we can use it as the to-do for the Friday handoff.

Karthik's short checklist (network & infra):
- CIDR blocks: please confirm VPC CIDR(s) and any overlapping ranges with Redwood's peering subnets. If overlapping, we require NATing or a dedicated transit.
- BGP / Peering: if using cloud interconnect, provide ASN and local preference; otherwise we'll do VPC peering with explicit route maps.
- Egress: list of IPs (or IP ranges) that must be allowed to authenticate to Redwood monitoring endpoints (expected ports: 443 outbound to 3 endpoints).
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TLS to these FQDNs and ports: runtime.redwood.ai:443, metrics.redwood.ai:443, keymgt.redwood.ai:443. We will provide IPs as fallback.
- Service accounts: name format (medico-redwood-<env>-sa), and at minimum roles: storage.objects.get, kms:decrypt (restricted to key ARN), logging.writer.
- KMS: please share key thumbprint/hash for us to allow cross-account decrypt if using CMEK.
- MTU & Jumbo frames: confirm if packets are MTU 1500 or larger; if >1500 we need to validate kernel path for large frames.
- Proxy/inspection: if traffic is inspected, share the CA cert so our runtime can validate TLS.
- Monitoring endpoints: will you allow push from Redwood, or should we pull logs from your syslog?

Evidence we typically collect before the smoke activation: one TCP handshake to runtime (443), TLS cert chain verification, simple token auth exchange, and a sample KV write/read. If you can run a quick connectivity test and drop results in the shared Drive link before July 6, we can accelerate.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Maya / Karthik — thanks for the checklist and clarity.

Forwarding the first batch of artifacts for your intake: medico_sow_v3.docx, network_diagram_v2.pdf, and a small tarball of baseline connectivity logs (connectivity-logs.zip). See the Drive link for screenshots of our router ACLs.

Brief replies to checkboxes: 
- CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 (app), 10.20.0.0/16 (infra). No overlaps with Redwood's peering ranges.
- Egress: we'll provide a static NAT pool (3 IPs) for outbound traffic to Redwood; range will be confirmed July 5 morning.
- Service account: will create medico-redwood-prod-sa with the roles you specified and share bindings.
- KMS: using CMEK; I'll upload the key thumbprint to the Drive link and share access with the redwood-infra service account.
- Packet MTU: default 1500. No packet inspection on these paths.

We are good to go for the July 6 10:00am PT call. I'll include our security engineer (cc'd) for the KMS and audit log conversation.
